correctness.rationale: For each rook cell, selected closed-neighborhood count equals its selected row degree plus selected column degree minus its own membership indicator. Maximum row and column degrees can sum only to at most four; the equality case forces all intersections of maximum-degree rows and columns to be selected. The resulting exhaustive component case split proves the five-family partition, counting formula, maximum-size law and wide-rectangle extremizers. Independent direct finite enumeration, formula computation and component inspection agree; they are checks rather than the infinite proof.

value.rationale: An exact all-cardinality polynomial and exhaustive component theorem for an infinite canonical Cartesian-product family are substantive structural results. The sharply piecewise maximum law shows only a two-unit improvement beyond matching size on square boards but doubling under large aspect ratio. This makes the precise capacity-three condition mathematically informative rather than a routine substitution.
